decisions.reason: The report explicitly separates the two projections: clipboardText/InputState.draft where chips expand to their clipboard form and Occurrence.offset/length live, versus detectText where each chip is one U+FFFC and which insertReference/consumeToken splice, grounding this in the contract types and the facade's detectText.slice and $replaceDetectSpanWith* calls; it also notes plain text and the separating space count normally, so a chip-free document makes the spaces coincide.

It pins snapshot.draft.length in add() as the clipboard-space span sent to insertReference, explains paste #1 succeeds only because 0 is valid in both spaces on an empty composer, and paste #2 sends 29 against a 2-character detect document so the splice fails (revision CAS passes due to re-snapshot), turning the false return into the changed-composer toast; it explicitly rejects a real concurrent edit and derives the first-works/later-fails signature from the projections diverging by length-1 after the first chip.

It traces remove() passing clipboard-space occurrence.offset/length as a [0,28) span to consumeToken's detect-space guard, notes the false return is never inspected and records.delete runs unconditionally, so the chip stays while the renderer's record===undefined branch prints 'unavailable'; it ties both symptoms to the same coordinate mismatch rather than an upload failure, and flags the ?? 1 default as a detect-space misread.

It derives detectPos(p) = p − Σ(o.length − 1) from the host sources and applies concrete code at both call sites: insertion at draft end reduces over all occurrences (29−27=2 checked against the capture), and removal maps occurrence.offset then uses a one-detect-character span (end = start + 1); both spans keep draftRev, records are retired only after a true consumption result (early return keeps the record on false), and the insert path keeps its transactional cleanup.

The plan asserts two successive pastes with both chips present (occurrences, records, draft and detect text), then removal steps where a chip with preceding chips is deleted and composer occurrence, dock chip and record disappear together while the other chip's label is unchanged, plus valid extras: declined-consumption bookkeeping, last-chip/empty-again and reset-by-removal variants, order independence, text-adjacent removal, and unit invariants on span bounds and return-value checks.
